Under baseline conditions, school enrollments in the impact area communities will increase significantly as a result of natural population growth. These schools will require additional facilities and personnel, necessitating bond issues and increased mill levies for operation. As previously indicated this is not expected to occur in rural school districts.
Impacts of Coal Development - The impacts of coal development in the recent past have fallen primarily on three governmental units: Big Horn County, Hardin, and the Hardin School Districts. Whether the future effects of mining will be beneficial or detrimental will depend in part on the amount of revenue derived from the presence of coal mining for each jurisdiction, and on the residential choices of the in-migrants. Tables 29 to 32 in Appendix I indicate that large tax payments will be made to county and state governments. In addition, some property tax increases will accrue to the Hardin School Districts, although estimates are not easily obtained because mill levies fluctuate widely. Although some of the Montana Coal Severance Tax receipts will be available to other local governments (see following section), most revenue from coal development in Big Horn County will accrue to the state and county governments.
